title: Cotangent sheaf model and its standard functoriality comparison
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Let $\mathcal C_{B/A}$ be the opposite category of polynomial $A$-algebras $P$ equipped with an $A$-algebra map $P\to B$, whose morphisms before taking opposites are $A$-algebra maps commuting with augmentations. Use a common infinite variable-cardinality bound containing all rings involved and a small skeleton in [def-weil-size-convention], with identity-cover topology. Let $\mathcal O(P\to B)=P$, with augmentation $\mathcal O\to\underline B$, and define the $\underline B$-module presheaf $F_{B/A}(P\to B)=\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_P B$ with restriction maps induced by algebra maps and universal differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\pi:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_{B/A}),\underline B)\to(*,B)$ and its derived lower shriek be as in [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar]. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$\theta_{B/A}:L\pi_!F_{B/A}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{B/A}$$
in $D(B)$, where $L_{B/A}$ is the standard simplicial cotangent complex of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. More generally, for every module presheaf $F$ and every polynomial resolution $P_\bullet\to B$ in that node, $L\pi_!F$ is canonically identified with the alternating differential complex $s(F(P_\bullet\to B))$, naturally in $F$ and in morphisms of augmented resolutions. On $F_{B/A}$ this agrees with that node's comparison isomorphism for polynomial resolutions.
For an arbitrary commutative square $A\to B$, $A'\to B'$, $a:A\to A'$, $b:B\to B'$, define $u:\mathcal C_{B/A}\to\mathcal C_{B'/A'}$ by $(P\to B)\mapsto(P\otimes_A A'\to B')$ and let $t:F_{B/A}\to u^{-1}F_{B'/A'}$ be the $b$-semilinear transformation
$$\mathrm dp\otimes r\longmapsto\mathrm d(p\otimes1)\otimes b(r).$$
If $T=L\pi_!(u,t)$ is the map represented by the bar-chain formula of [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar], then
$$\theta_{B'/A'}\,T=f^{\mathrm{std}}_{a,b}\,\theta_{B/A}$$
after restriction of scalars to $B$, where $f^{\mathrm{std}}_{a,b}$ is the canonical map induced by standard resolutions in [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. The identity is for all ring squares, without any injectivity or flatness assumption on $a$ or $b$.

source.place: Tags 08PS (lemma-identify-pi-shriek), 08PT (lemma-pi-shriek-standard), 08PU (lemma-compute-cotangent-complex), 08QI (remark-resolution), 08QL (section-functoriality), including the omitted agreement of sheaf and standard-resolution maps, isolated here as a supporting comparison lemma.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal D=\mathcal C_{B/A}^{op}$, the category of polynomial $A$-algebras augmented to $B$ in the statement. Use its chosen small skeleton and transport the resolutions to it; the stipulated common infinite bound contains the sets of generators of their terms and of the standard resolution. A presheaf on $\mathcal C_{B/A}$ is a covariant functor on $\mathcal D$. By [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar], $L\pi_!F$ is the left derived colimit of this functor. There is a sign convention to fix when using [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-colimit-computation]: the chain $U_n\to\cdots\to U_0$ in $\mathcal C$ becomes $T_0\to\cdots\to T_n$ in $\mathcal D$, with $T_i=U_i$. The former bar deletes the last vertex first, while the latter deletes the first vertex first. Thus $d_{\mathcal C,n}=(-1)^n d_{\mathcal D,n}$. Multiplication in degree $-n$ by $\lambda_n=(-1)^{n(n+1)/2}$ gives a chain isomorphism $j_F:K_{\mathcal C}(F)\to K_{\mathcal D}(F)$, since $\lambda_n=(-1)^n\lambda_{n-1}$. It is the identity in degree zero, respects augmentations, and commutes with every bar map induced by a functor and coefficient transformation. We use this explicit identification throughout.

source.place: Tags 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), 08PH (example-morphism-categories), 08Q9 (lemma-compute-by-cosimplicial-resolution); reversal of the bar face order written explicitly

proof.text: Let $P_\bullet\to B$ be any polynomial resolution specified in [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Regard it as a morphism of simplicial abelian groups to the constant simplicial group $B$. By the definition in that node every $P_n\to B$ is surjective, so the morphism is termwise surjective. The alternating complex $s(B)$ of constant $B$ has differential $\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i\mathrm{id}_B$ from degree $n$, which is zero for odd $n$ and the identity for even $n\geq2$; hence $H_0(s(B))=B$, $H_n(s(B))=0$ for $n\geq1$, and $s(B)\to B[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Since $s(P_\bullet)\to B[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the definition of resolution and factors through $s(B)$, the map $s(P_\bullet)\to s(B)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. By [lem-trf-surjective-qis-simplicial-group-trivial-kan] (Stacks Tag 08P1) the underlying map of simplicial sets $P_\bullet\to B$ is a trivial Kan fibration in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]: surjective on vertices, with boundary fillers for all $n\geq1$. This applies to the standard resolution too, since [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] states that it is a resolution, and its terms surject onto $B$ by that definition.

For an object $T=A[E]\to B$ of $\mathcal D$, a simplex of $S_T=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(T,P_\bullet)$ is a choice, for each $e\in E$, of a simplex of $P_\bullet$ mapping to the prescribed element $\epsilon_T(e)$ of $B$. This follows from the universal property of a polynomial algebra and commutes with all simplicial operators. A lifting problem for $S_T\to *$ against $\partial\Delta[n]\hookrightarrow\Delta[n]$ therefore gives, for each generator, a boundary lifting problem for $P_\bullet\to B$ over the constant simplex $\epsilon_T(e)$. Step 2 and [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration] provide fillers; choose them for all generators and extend uniquely to an algebra map $T\to P_n$. For $n=0$ choose generator lifts by the same condition. Hence $S_T\to *$ is a trivial Kan fibration. By [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence] it is homotopy equivalent to a singleton. This includes the empty generator set and arbitrary sets of generators within the size bound.

source.place: Tag 08PS (lemma-identify-pi-shriek), representables expressed as choices of lifts of generators; simplicial Tag 08NS (lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy)

proof.text: Steps 1 and 3 verify the smallness and representable-contractibility hypotheses of [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-colimit-computation], with $R=B$, $Q=P_\bullet$, and the covariant functor corresponding to any module presheaf $F$. It gives $a_{P,F}:s(F(P_\bullet))\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf H(\mathcal D,F)$. Composing with the inverse of Step 1's bar identification gives $\alpha_{P,F}:s(F(P_\bullet))\xrightarrow{\sim}L\pi_!F$. Its naturality in $F$ and in augmented simplicial maps $P\to Q$ is the naturality asserted by that node; in particular $\alpha_{Q,F}s(F(h))=\alpha_{P,F}$. Inverting $\alpha_{P,F}$ proves the general resolution formula in the item. No flatness or exactness assumption on $F$ is used.

source.place: Tag 08Q9 (lemma-compute-by-cosimplicial-resolution), specialized as in cotangent Tags 08PS and 08QI

proof.text: The maps $dp\otimes r\mapsto d(v(p))\otimes r$ for an augmented algebra map $v:P\to Q$ define the coefficient functor $F_{B/A}$: additivity, the Leibniz relation, and the vanishing of differentials of elements of $A$ are preserved, using the defining relations in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. The tensor relation is preserved because both augmentations give the same action on $B$. Identity and composition hold on these generating symbols. For $P=P^{\mathrm{std}}$, [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] identifies $s(F_{B/A}(P))$ with its defining complex $L_{B/A}$. Define $\theta_{B/A}=\alpha_{\mathrm{std},F_{B/A}}^{-1}$. For any other resolution the induced comparison is $\theta_{B/A}\alpha_{P,F_{B/A}}$. These are the polynomial-resolution comparisons of Tags 08PU and 08QI: evaluate the sheaf on the standard resolution to define $L_{B/A}$, and identify its evaluation on any other resolution through the same $L\pi_!F_{B/A}$. This fixes the canonical comparison convention in [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], rather than choosing an arbitrary isomorphism. If the comparison of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] is formed on the larger category of all small augmented polynomial algebras rather than on the skeleton, the reindexing clause of [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-colimit-computation] for the inclusion $i$, identity coefficients and $k$ the transport isomorphism gives $a^{\mathrm{big}}_P=\mathbf H(i,\mathrm{id})a_P$ for $P$ and for the standard resolution alike, so $a_{\mathrm{std}}^{-1}a_P$ is the same in both.

source.place: Tags 08PU (lemma-compute-cotangent-complex) and 08QI (remark-resolution), with the defining complex of Tag 08PN

proof.text: For the arbitrary square $(a,b)$ in the statement, write $v:\mathcal D_{B/A}\to\mathcal D_{B'/A'}$ for $P\mapsto P\otimes_A A'$; its opposite is $u$. It lands in polynomial presentations: $A[E]\otimes_A A'\simeq A'[E]$, with the inverse maps fixing the variables and coefficients, and the augmentation sends $p\otimes a'$ to $b(\epsilon_P(p))a'$. The formula $t_P(dp\otimes r)=d(p\otimes1)\otimes b(r)$ respects the differential relations of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. It is balanced because $d(p\otimes1)(q\otimes1)\otimes b(r)=d(p\otimes1)\otimes b(\epsilon_P(q)r)$, and is $b$-semilinear. For an augmented map $h:P\to Q$, both naturality composites send $dp\otimes r$ to $d(h(p)\otimes1)\otimes b(r)$. Thus this is the coefficient transformation for the general reindexing comparison, without conditions on $a,b$.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), category functor u and the coefficient transformation

proof.text: Let $P=P^{\mathrm{std}}(B/A)$ and $P'=P^{\mathrm{std}}(B'/A')$. The standard semilinear augmented simplicial map $h:P\to P'$ is supplied by [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Its extension $k:vP\to P'$ sends $p\otimes a'$ to $h(p)a'$. It is well defined by $a$-semilinearity; it commutes with each simplicial operator and augmentation because $h$ does. The composite coefficient map in degree $n$ is explicitly $F_{B'/A'}(k_n)t_{P_n}(dp\otimes r)=d(h_n(p))\otimes b(r)$. Therefore its alternating chain map is precisely the standard differential-complex map $f^{\mathrm{std}}_{a,b}$ in that node. This uses only the construction of $k$ and the differential relations in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials].

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), explicit standard-resolution maps and their differential maps

proof.text: Apply the reindexing clause of [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-colimit-computation] to $v,t,k$ of Steps 6 and 7. Both endpoints $P,P'$ satisfy its hypothesis by Step 3. It gives $a_{P',F'}f^{\mathrm{std}}_{a,b}=\mathbf H(v,t)a_{P,F}$ after restriction to $B$. By the bar-chain formula in [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar], and the sign identification of Step 1, $\mathbf H(v,t)$ corresponds exactly to the specified map $T=L\pi_!(u,t)$: both send a chain with coefficient $x$ to its image chain with coefficient $t(x)$, and the scalar $\lambda_n$ commutes with this operation. Thus $\alpha_{P',F'}f^{\mathrm{std}}_{a,b}=T\alpha_{P,F}$. Multiply on the left by $\alpha_{P',F'}^{-1}$ and on the right by $\alpha_{P,F}^{-1}$ to obtain $\theta_{B'/A'}T=f^{\mathrm{std}}_{a,b}\theta_{B/A}$. Restriction of scalars here is degreewise restriction on these bar models, as expressly provided by the comparison node. Its naturality clause requires no contractibility of $vP$; in particular nothing assumes $P\otimes_A A'\to B'$ to be a resolution. This proves the identity for every ring square.
